newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Over 500 laid off at Hong Kong power project.
newsitem.headline: Over 500 laid off at Hong Kong power project.

text.p: More than 500 workers have been laid off at China Light and Power Co Ltd's Black Point power plant project after a government request for deferment, Hong Kong radio and television said on Saturday.
China Light was asked by the Hong Kong government last week to defer the building of the second phase of the eight-unit power station because of slow growth in electricity demand.
"More than 500 workers for the Black Point power station project have been laid off. They received their notice on Friday," ATV television news said.
It did not name which of China Light's contractors was involved. China Light officials were unavailable to comment on Saturday.
The company said earlier that the plant was expected to cost HK$24 billion (US$3.1 billion) and that 84 percent was already committed.

Construction of the 2,496-megawatt gas-fired power plant was originally approved by the government in two phases, in 1992 and 1994. The first phase has been completed, and China Light officials have said construction and capital commitments related to the second phase were already in an advanced stage.
